title: ADR Registry / Index
description: The ADR registry for docs/adr/, organized by DDD bounded context (top-level category key) and feature/vertical-slice (optional second segment). This file is the single ADR index — each ADR is listed once with its path, Status, and a one-line Key Decision summary, so the README keeps NO separate ADR list. It carries an optional advisory subdomainType (core/supporting/generic) per context. The link between an ADR and the code that implements it is not stored here — agents locate the relevant code by reading the ADR and searching the repo. adr-writer is standalone: this file records no ALPS/PRD reference. A feature name may originate from an ALPS Section 7 feature when it was imported once via feature-to-adr, but the mapping treats it as a plain name and does not point back at the PRD. Note: draft-07 cannot express the cross-entry invariants (unique adr path across the whole file, dependsOn references an existing key, no self-edge, acyclic, mapping status mirrors the ADR body) — those are enforced by scripts/adr-lint-lib.mjs / adr-structure-lint.mjs (R8/R16) and adr-sync step 6, not this schema.

$schema.description: Optional JSON Schema pointer; ignored by the tools but allowed so editors can resolve validation.

categories.description: Map of category id (kebab-case) to mapping entry. Category id matches the ADR directory path under docs/adr/. The top segment is a DDD bounded context / subdomain named with the domain expert's ubiquitous-language term (e.g., 'identity', 'ordering'); the optional second segment is a user-perceived feature / vertical slice (e.g., 'identity/login'). At most two segments — no deeper nesting; the propertyNames.pattern enforces the ≤2-kebab-segment shape so a 3-segment key ('identity/login/social') or an uppercase key ('F1') is rejected at validation time, not just in prose. When a context holds exactly one feature the second segment is elided and a single-segment key means context==feature (legacy/flat layout, e.g. 'auth'). Keys are derived from the feature NAME. A PRD Feature ID is never used as a key (and is not stored anywhere in this file) — the folder need not be named 'f1', and /adr-impl resolves a target by its category key, not by a Feature ID. Only when no meaningful kebab name exists (e.g. a purely numeric workshop id) is a lowercased id used as a fallback single-segment key. See structure.md '디렉토리 구조' and 'ADR 레지스트리 (.mapping.json)'.

feature.description: Human-readable feature name (for feature-level entries) or bounded-context name (for context-level entries). When the category was imported once from an ALPS Section 7 feature this is that feature's name, but adr-writer treats it as a plain label — it is not a PRD reference.

subdomainType.description: DDD subdomain classification of the bounded context this category belongs to. Advisory metadata only — never a hard gate and never a folder tier. Feature contexts are typically core/supporting; system-wide cross-cutting contexts (infra/integration/security/platform/data) are generic. Place it on the context-level entry (the top-folder entry, or a single-feature flat entry); per-feature sub-folder entries inherit the parent context's type conceptually and may omit it. Surfaced by adr-sync and the hook snapshot as advisory context (e.g. grouping by domain, 'generic — candidate for off-the-shelf'), never enforced. Omit when unknown.

adrs.description: The ADRs recorded under this category. Each item indexes one ADR by path + its current Status + a one-line Key Decision summary — this array IS the ADR index (the README carries no separate ADR list). Each path appears exactly once across the whole file. MAY be empty ([]) for a context-level grouping entry that holds no context-direct (cross-cutting) ADR — its feature sub-folder entries carry the actual ADRs (e.g. an 'identity' entry with adrs:[] alongside 'identity/login' and 'identity/signup'). Feature/flat entries normally have at least one item. adr-structure-lint additionally requires every on-disk NNNN-*.md to appear here exactly once, every path here to resolve on disk, and every item's status to mirror the ADR body's ## Status line.

path.description: Path to the ADR markdown file, relative to the repo root (e.g. docs/adr/identity/login/0001-password-policy.md).

status.description: The ADR's current Status, mirroring the ADR body's ## Status line: 'Proposed' | 'Accepted (YYYY-MM-DD)' | 'Deprecated (YYYY-MM-DD)' | 'Superseded by [ADR ...](...)'. This is the single index of status — adr-impl/adr-sync update it in lockstep with the body, and adr-structure-lint verifies the two agree.

summary.description: One-line Key Decision summary — the entry point for /adr-sync --quick and what the hook renders after the path. Recommended for every ADR; omitting it is advisory (adr-structure-lint warns).

dependsOn.description: Category ids this category depends on (prerequisites). Recorded by adr-new when the author names a prerequisite ADR, or backfilled once by feature-to-adr from an ALPS Section 6.3 dependency graph (edge 'this --depends on--> X' becomes X in this list). Read by adr-impl to implement prerequisite ADRs first, and validated by adr-sync. Uses the same key namespace as 'categories' (single-segment or two-segment context/feature keys). Edges MAY cross bounded-context boundaries (e.g. an ordering/checkout feature depending on an identity/login feature is a normal DDD context relationship). Must reference existing category keys; keep acyclic (no self-edge).

tableDocs.description: Paths to schema/table documents (e.g., docs/tables/*.md, prisma/schema.prisma) that must stay bidirectionally linked with ADRs in this category. Used by the authoring-rules DB schema co-change rule and by adr-sync auxiliary doc check.
